title: Korean Garlic Beef Bowls
seoTitle: Korean Beef Rice Bowls | Firefighter Meal
shortDescription: Bulgogi-style ground beef over rice with quick cucumber pickle
subtitle: Bulgogi-style ground beef over rice with quick cucumber pickle
description: Ground beef caramelizes in a soy-sesame-ginger glaze with grated pear for tenderness. Served over steamed rice with scallions, sesame seeds, and quick pickled cucumber.

steps.title: Gather ingredients and equipment
steps.instruction: Line up every ingredient for Korean Garlic Beef Bowls in the order you will cook — measure spices into ramekins, trim proteins on a dedicated board, and set tongs, thermometers, and hotel pans within arm's reach before any heat goes on.

steps.title: Preheat ovens and surfaces
steps.instruction: Preheat ovens, griddles, or grills to recipe temp before the crew arrives — cold equipment extends cook time and dries out batch beef. Confirm burners ignite evenly and sheet pans are greased or lined.

steps.title: Quick pickle cucumbers
steps.instruction: Toss cucumber slices with rice vinegar and a pinch of salt. Refrigerate while cooking so they stay crisp-tender with a bright tang. Plan about 5 minutes for this step at crew scale. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Cook rice
steps.instruction: Rinse jasmine rice and cook per package directions until fluffy grains separate easily with a fork, not sticky or gummy. Plan about 20 minutes for this step at crew scale. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Mix bulgogi-style sauce
steps.instruction: Whisk soy sauce, brown sugar, sesame oil, ginger, garlic, and grated pear until sugar dissolves and mixture smells sweet-savory. Plan about 5 minutes for this step at crew scale. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Brown beef in batches
steps.instruction: Cook ground beef over medium-high in a large skillet 8–10 minutes per batch until deeply browned and crumbly with crisp edges, not gray and steaming. Target 145°F for medium beef, 160°F for ground at the thickest part before moving to the next batch. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Verify safe internal temps
steps.instruction: Spot-check the thickest pieces with an instant-read thermometer — target 145°F for medium beef, 160°F for ground. If any piece reads low, return it to heat immediately rather than holding under temp on the line.

steps.title: Glaze and build bowls
steps.instruction: Return all beef to pan, pour sauce, simmer 3–4 minutes until glaze coats meat and pan looks shiny, not soupy. Serve over rice with pickles and scallions. Maintain a steady simmer — bubbles should break the surface without a rolling boil that shreds delicate proteins. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

proTips: Grated pear tenderizes lean beef—do not skip even if it feels unusual.
Offer gochujang at the line for crews who want fermented heat.
Drain excess fat after browning so the glaze stays glossy.
tonightSpread: Kimchi or quick cabbage slaw for crunch.
leftovers: Beef in lettuce cups next day with extra cucumber pickle.
Fried rice with leftover beef, egg, and frozen peas.
whyCrewsLikeIt: Big flavor without a marinade wait. Bowl format lets crew customize heat and keeps service moving on busy nights.
mealPrepNotes: Mix sauce and slice cucumbers the night before. Marinate beef up to 4 hours for deeper flavor. Station: Cook rice first in a cooker so the skillet stays free for beef batches. Station: Sear beef in two batches—crowded meat steams instead of browning. Station: Set bowl line: rice, beef, cucumber, kimchi optional, sesame and scallion.
